content.text:
I submitted **index 268 (Bi 0.40, Cu 0.19, V 0.41)**. Its photocurrent of **3.1×10⁻⁷ A** was the best of the three merit measurements. With only three measurements across 275 compositions, I can't say whether it is the best composition in the library.

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | 0.16 / 0.27 / 0.57 (more V than Bi or Cu) | 1.6×10⁻⁷ |
| **268** | 0.40 / 0.19 / 0.41 (Bi and V about equal) | **3.1×10⁻⁷** |
| 93 | 0.44 / 0.20 / 0.36 (slightly more Bi than V) | 4×10⁻⁸ |

- **Reading of the trend:** photocurrent was highest where Bi and V are about equal, which fits a BiVO4-type phase with some Cu. Moving to extra V or extra Bi lowered it.
- **Model checks were weak evidence:** each merit measurement had to cite a model check first. I couldn't read the phase list because it was too large for the output, so I found only one usable phase ID, V2O5. MACE puts it on the stability hull, and MEGNet predicts a 2.83 eV band gap. That gap is above the 2.4 eV photon energy, which suggests extra V absorbs poorly. None of these checks tested a Bi–Cu–V phase directly.
- **Unused tools:** I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements. The Gaussian-process suggestions weren't helpful with so few data points, so I didn't follow them.
